Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates dextrocardia (heart on the right) and a gastric bubble on the right, confirming situs inversus totalis. In Kartagener's syndrome with situs inversus, the anatomical reversal leads to bronchiectatic changes that are typically bilateral but more pronounced on the left side (the morphological right lung), which corresponds to the findings described in option F.
